cases.note: CONFIRMED is genuinely produced by GhostToolsAdapter.invoke() (test-proven, TestGhostToolsAdapterThroughRealPipeline), returned via a loop variable bound by iterating a module-level tuple. removed_from_library because the prior commit's if/elif cascade had it as an inline attribute-access literal, which counts as production; the table refactor that replaced the cascade (asked for, MAJOR ghost-0f0192120c82) moved it into a module-level constant collection, which ghost_buster's own v1.7.6 fix deliberately excludes from counting as production. A necessary side effect of the dedup, not a regression in behavior. Restructuring back into branches to satisfy the detector would reintroduce the exact duplication it was asked to remove.

GhostToolsStatus.CONFIRMED_BY_REVIEW is declared so a value read back from real ghost_tools data (a casefile, a human review) has somewhere correct to land -- same pattern ghost_tools' own schema.py documents for this exact member. Not dead; arrives from data, never as a literal in this codebase.

GhostToolsStatus.SUPPRESSED is real, active vocabulary in ghost_tools' own triage/baseline flow. Unreachable here only because GhostToolsAdapter is a documented placeholder that doesn't call Baseline.accept(). Resolves when the adapter becomes real.

InnovationOSDecision.EVALUATED has no real Innovation OS repository in scope to verify against. Unverified, not confirmed dead -- kept per ghost_tools' own precedent of not deleting a member on the strength of an absence that might be this checkout's, not the vocabulary's.

Same root cause as CONFIRMED: SwizzleVerdict.CONJURED was an inline literal in the pre-refactor cascade, now a module-level table key. SwizzleAdapter never actually returned CONJURED before or after this change -- its production status only ever reflected the cascade's literal shape, not real reachability.
Same as CONJURED: SwizzleVerdict.DISMISSED's removed_from_library reading tracks the cascade-to-table refactor, not a behavior change. SwizzleAdapter's placeholder never produced it either way.

SwizzleVerdict.MISNAMED is real, active vocabulary in SWIZZLE's own verdict.py. Unreachable here only because SwizzleAdapter is a documented placeholder returning 2 of 6 verdicts. Resolves when the adapter becomes real.
SwizzleVerdict.UNSUMMONED is real, active vocabulary in SWIZZLE's own run.py/invoke.py (means the harness itself failed to run). Same placeholder-adapter gap as MISNAMED.

WizzleForensics.NEVER_PRODUCED arrives only via WizzleAdapter's real path, WizzleForensics(result.value) from ghost_buster.forensics.provenance() -- a non-literal constructor call, by design. Verified end-to-end against ghost_tools' own repo in tests/test_outcomes.py.
WizzleForensics.RELOCATED_TO_TESTS: same as NEVER_PRODUCED, arrives from the real provenance() call, never as a literal here.
WizzleForensics.REMOVED_FROM_LIBRARY: same as NEVER_PRODUCED, arrives from the real provenance() call, never as a literal here.

cns_resolve's enum-or-string duplication is intentional defensive shape for the real cns.gate.resolve contract, and the function has zero call sites anywhere in this repo (confirmed by full-repo grep). No live bug, nothing to fix; a table refactor here would be cleanup with no correctness payoff, unlike cns_canonicalize's twin which was fixed because it had actually drifted.

ghost-buster (ghost_tools) is a deliberately optional import for WizzleAdapter's real-mode forensics check, same try/except shape as cns.gate. Not declared as a hard dependency on purpose: there is no installable URL for it and CI never has it checked out, so the fallback path (honest UNKNOWN) is what CI actually exercises and is tested for.
